newsitem.title: ITALY: VETERAN GALGANI RESIGNS AS HEAD OF ITALIAN TENNIS.
newsitem.headline: VETERAN GALGANI RESIGNS AS HEAD OF ITALIAN TENNIS.

text.p: Paolo Galgani, the powerful head of Italian tennis for over 20 years, said on Friday he would resign after stinging attacks on his management style from the media, players and coaching staff.
After a special meeting of the Italian tennis federation, Galgani told reporters the current board would step down in November.
The move could open the way for the return of former Italian Davis Cup captain Adriano Panatta, who quit last month, jeopardising the team's world group semifinal against Sweden.

Panatta, whose squad scored a surprise victory over Spain in the quarter-finals in April, said he could not continue to work with Galgani after the president refused to renew his contract as technical director.

Galgani, whose term as Italian tennis federation president was to run until 2000, had been under mounting pressure to resign from numerous critics who said his domineering management was hurting the sport.

Friday's special meeting of the federation was called by Italian Olympic Committee president Mario Pescante after Sports Minister Walter Veltroni expressed concern for the future of the Davis Cup campaign.
Some of the squad had pledged loyalty to Panatta following his resignation and hinted they might consider pulling out of the semifinals.
Panatta, who won the French Open in 1976, said he would return to the squad only if Galgani resigned.

The federation said on Friday another captain would probably take his place for the semifinal in Sweden on September 19-21, the second time in as many years Italy has reached the last four of the Davis Cup world group.
Last year they were knocked out in the semifinals by France after leading for most of the match.
